title: Bound to the Mast
blurb: Sail past the Sirens. One sings, one is tied up, one must keep rowing.

characters.name: Odysseus
characters.description: Tied to the mast and losing his mind.

characters.name: Eurylochus
characters.description: First mate. Ears full of beeswax.

lines.text: Bind me to the mast, hand and foot, and if I beg you to set me free, bind me all the tighter.
lines.direction: Arms behind your back, as if tied.

lines.text: Come here, renowned Odysseus, honour to the Achaean name. Stay your ship and listen to our voices.
lines.direction: Beckon slowly. Sing it if you dare.

lines.text: No one ever sailed past us without staying to hear our sweet song, and he went on his way a wiser man.
Untie me! Untie me, I command you! I must hear the rest of their song!
Row harder, men! Bind him tighter! Do not look back!
lines.direction: Row like your life depends on it. It does.

lines.text: The song is fading. Thank you, Eurylochus. You have saved us all.

source: Homer, The Odyssey, tr. Samuel Butler (public domain), adapted
